subject: Novus: follow-up on hosting vs reserved capacity — cost scenarios and next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zhang <c.zhang@novushealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 15:18:00 -0700
Subject: Novus: follow-up on hosting vs reserved capacity — cost scenarios and next steps

Hi Claire — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we stay aligned: 

Summary of customer requirements (as I heard them):
- Primary use: consumer-facing summaries and search for patient-facing app (low latency on reads, moderate generation volume)
- Expected baseline: ~120M tokens/month, with spikes to ~8k QPS sustained over 5–10m windows during product events
- Compliance: SOC2 required; consider VPC/private options for logs and KMS integration
- Launch target: Q4 2027 (pilot in Sept)

Options we reviewed and high-level implications:
1) Hosted API (Redwood hosted) — fastest to go live, pay-per-token. Good for unpredictable spikes but higher marginal cost at scale.
2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) — monthly GPU commit with predictable unit cost for tokens; cheaper at steady-state but requires a commit and capacity planning.
3) Private (VPC/on-prem) — for strict compliance and data residency; higher upfront ops and licensing.

Primary cost drivers to confirm: average sequence length, prompt vs completion token split, percent cacheable prefixes, and 95th percentile latency requirement. Those determine whether reserved GPU economics beat per-token pricing.

As next steps we propose: 
- Claire: share a 2–3 month representative token/sample traffic CSV (time-series) so we can run the break-even model.
- Redwood (me + Marissa): prepare 2 cost scenarios (hosted per-token vs 3 commit sizes for Dedicated) and one Private installation estimate. We'll include run-rate break-even and suggested commit band.
- Schedule a 30-min model walkthrough next week to agree assumptions.

I attached a short one-pager (redwood-quick-sla.pdf) that outlines SLA tiers and burst handling. I will share an editable cost spreadsheet once we have the token profile.

Thanks — Sean
Sean Gallagher
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Sean — good summary and appreciated the clear options. A few clarifications from our side before you build scenarios: 

1) Token profile: we'll provide a 7-day sample export by EOD Thu (includes prompt/completion tags). Expect average sequence length ~160 tokens, prompt:completion split ~1:2.
2) Spikes: the 8k QPS number is peak sustained for ~10 minutes during product notifications; typical daily peak is ~800 qps.
3) Compliance: SOC2 Type II in place. For VPC/on-prem we will need HSM/KMS integration and an option to retain full audit logs for 2 years.
4) Procurement: please copy procurement on any pricing docs. They also asked for a short list of customers with a similar Private install reference.

Two specific asks for your modeling: 
- Please include a simple break-even chart that shows at what monthly token volume the Dedicated reserved option becomes cheaper than Hosted per-token (assume 4:1 caching factor for common prefixes).
- Show an example commit profile: low (50% of projected steady-state), mid (100%), high (150%) and the expected unit token cost in each.

We'll aim to have the data file to you tomorrow. If you can include a rough PO process timeline for the U.S. market that helps procurement.

Best,

Subject: Re: Novus: follow-up on hosting vs reserved capacity — cost scenarios and next steps

Claire — thanks for the quick clarifications. I attached a starter cost model (novus-cost-scenarios.xlsx) with three tabs: Hosted_Base, Dedicated_commits, and Private_onprem_estimate. High-level notes from the workbook: 

- Hosted_Base: we used your preliminary avg sequence (160 tokens) and a mixture of prompt/completion split. Base hosted per-token rate (est) = $0.0009 per generated token (volume-discount tiers included).
- Dedicated_commits: modeled three commit bands (small: 1x A100-equivalent GPU pool, mid: 3 GPUs, large: 6 GPUs) with assumed utilization rates. At ~120M tokens/month, mid-commit yields ~30% lower unit cost vs hosted; at >=250M tokens/month the large commit is materially cheaper.
- Private_onprem_estimate: includes license fee + one-time infra setup + estimated on-call support. Break-even for on-prem vs dedicated depends heavily on ops costs and SKUs; we flagged key sensitivities in the sheet.

Quick assumptions called out in the sheet (please review): tokenization model, average token/sec per GPU, cache hit rates (we included a 4x cacheable prefix assumption per your ask), and burst handling (burst capacity billed as overage or short-term spot in Dedicated).

Next steps I propose: 
- You + procurement: confirm the sample CSV by EOD tomorrow.
- Marissa: I'll loop you in to arrange a 30-min cost walkthrough — propose Mon 28 Jun 10:00am PT or Tue 29 Jun 1:00pm PT.
- Post-walkthrough: we'll provide a draft commercial term sheet + sample SOW for a pilot (includes SLAs, on-call windows, and data handling).

Attachment: novus-cost-scenarios.xlsx (editable spreadsheet).

Let me know which walkthrough time works — I'll send a calendar invite and include the procurement contact.

Thanks — Sean
Sean Gallagher
